observations.name: desktop
observations.text:
HUMANS CAN HAVE FREE WILL · DANIEL DENNETT
"We want our will to be determined by the facts and by our values."

Dennett argues that worthwhile agency requires sensitivity to reasons and values, rather than a will detached from causation.

"

observations.name: desktop
observations.text:
HUMANS DO NOT HAVE FREE WILL · ROBERT SAPOLSKY
"self-control is as biological of a trait as is your eye color."

Sapolsky challenges Dennett’s capacity account by locating executive control in unchosen biological development and environmental history.

"
